name: Null and dominant energy conditions for a thin-shell surface stress (NEC: sigma + p >= 0; DEC: sigma >= 0 and sigma >= |p|)

source.located: Definition: Hawking & Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time (CUP 1973) sec. 4.3 -- pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Read in two restatements. (i) The principal-pressure (type-I) forms: F.S.N. Lobo, 'Exotic solutions in General Relativity: traversable wormholes and warp drive spacetimes', arXiv:0710.4474v1 (2007), sec. II.F.1, eqs (62)-(70): NEC 'for all i, rho + p_i >= 0' (64); WEC 'rho >= 0 and for all i, rho + p_i >= 0' (66); DEC 'rho >= 0 and for all i, p_i in [-rho, +rho]' (70). (ii) The thin-shell forms themselves, in exactly the tree's notation: C. Choi & R.E. Grady, 'Sharp Tangential NEC Minimization and Israel Surface Layers in Schwarzschild Mass Interpolations', arXiv:2608.09963v1 (26 Jul 2026), Remark 7.6: 'For a surface stress tensor S^A_B = diag(-sigma, p, p) the shell null, weak, and dominant conditions read sigma + p >= 0; sigma >= 0 and sigma + p >= 0; and sigma >= 0 and |p| <= sigma.' The Lanczos/Israel sigma and p the conditions are applied to were audited by the sibling israel-lanczos-poisson-visser-thin-shell.json (Poisson-Visser gr-qc/9506083 eqs 6-8; Ishak-Lake gr-qc/0108058 eq 5) and are not re-read here; they are re-derived in sympy below.

published_statement: Type-I forms (Lobo 2007, restating Hawking-Ellis via Visser [15]), for T^{mu nu} = diag(rho, p_1, p_2, p_3): NEC: for all i, rho + p_i >= 0 (eq 64). WEC: rho >= 0 and for all i, rho + p_i >= 0 (eq 66). DEC: T_{mu nu}U^mu U^nu >= 0 and T^{mu nu}U_nu not spacelike (eq 69), i.e. rho >= 0 and for all i, p_i in [-rho, +rho] (eq 70). Thin-shell forms (Choi-Grady 2026, Remark 7.6): for S^A_B = diag(-sigma, p, p), 'the shell null, weak, and dominant conditions read sigma + p >= 0; sigma >= 0 and sigma + p >= 0; and sigma >= 0 and |p| <= sigma.' The same paper's title and sec. 2 call sigma + p (rho + p_t in the bulk) the TANGENTIAL NEC.
published_hypotheses: Pointwise classical conditions on a stress-energy tensor (Lobo 2007 sec. II.F.1: 'classical forms of matter are believed to obey these energy conditions ... violated by certain quantum fields').
Type-I (diagonalisable) stress tensor with principal pressures p_i (Lobo eq 62).

Thin-shell forms: 2+1 surface stress S^A_B = diag(-sigma, p, p), isotropic tangential pressure, conditions evaluated on the shell's world-volume with the induced metric (Choi-Grady Remark 7.6: 'shell null, weak, and dominant conditions').
The conditions are evaluated on the given (here static) sigma, p; nothing about perturbed configurations is asserted by the definitions.
hypothesis_drift: NEC SCOPE UNNAMED (stability.py:150-151 nec_holds; printed NEC column stability.py:228-232 and report 291-298). The tree's 'NEC' sigma + p >= 0 is exactly the published SHELL (tangential, 2+1) null condition (Choi-Grady Remark 7.6), but the tree does not carry the 'shell/tangential' qualifier. As a statement about the 4D distributional stress tensor T = diag(sigma, 0, p, p) delta(l) -- zero normal pressure -- the Hawking-Ellis NEC in Lobo's form (eq 64, rho + p_i >= 0 for EVERY i, including the normal direction with p_n = 0) requires sigma >= 0 AND sigma + p >= 0, i.e. the surface WEC. Machine-checked (z3, section D3), with an explicit counterexample (D5): sigma = -1, p = 2 passes nec_holds while the radial null vector k = (1,1,0,0) gives T_kk = sigma < 0. Consequence for the tree: none. The device has sigma > 0 for every m/R > 0 (z3, section B), where the two notions coincide, and nothing rests on nec_holds alone; the verdict rests on the DEC, which implies the 4D NEC (z3, D 'surface DEC => 4D NEC').

DEC: NO DRIFT. stability.py:145-147 dec_holds 's >= 0 and s >= abs(p)' is Choi-Grady's shell DEC and Lobo's eq (70) with the tangential p_i; z3 (D1) shows it is also EXACTLY the 4D DEC of the distributional tensor (the normal pressure 0 lies in [-sigma, sigma] once sigma >= 0, and the energy flux of a tangential stress is tangential). So the surface/4D ambiguity that affects the NEC does not affect the DEC the verdict uses.

SCOPE UNDERSTATED, NOT OVERSTATED (stability.py:35-36 'at every compactness tested'; :304-306 'at every compactness measured'; selftest :238-239 tests m/R in {0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 2.0}, report tests {0.01,...,1.0}). The re-derivation proves sigma > 0, p < 0 and sigma - |p| = sigma + p > 0 for EVERY m/R > 0 in closed form (sympy identities + z3 quantified over the reals), with |p|/sigma = x(2-3x)/8 + O(x^3) -> 1/4 as x -> oo, so the DEC margin never drops below 3/4 sigma. The tree's finite claim is true and generalises; it is recorded here only because a finite-sample claim is what the tree states.

STATIC ONLY (unnamed, no consequence for the statement as used). The conditions are checked at the static Lanczos values sigma_0, p_0 (stability.py:132-143). The stability analysis beside them evolves the shell with the EOS p' = beta^2 sigma' (stability.py:163-173) and reports beta^2_crit < 0; the DEC along a perturbed trajectory with a given beta^2 is not asserted by the tree and not checked here. The tree does not claim it, so it is scope, not a dropped hypothesis.

WORDING (stability.py:11, :24, :226, :304 'THE SHELL IS ORDINARY MATTER'). The published conditions are necessary conditions on a stress tensor; they do not certify that a matter model realising sigma > 0 with tension |p| <= sigma exists. The tree's evidence for 'ordinary' is exactly DEC satisfaction (stability.py:304-306), which the source supports as 'energy-condition-satisfying' and no further. Recorded as a discrepancy of wording, not a refutation.

CANONICAL LINE CITATION (canonical.json rests_on_it 'stability.py:238-239,304-306'): 238-239 is the selftest chk 'DOMINANT energy condition holds throughout'; the verdict prose is 303-306. Bookkeeping only.

D (z3): 4D DEC <=> surface DEC; 4D WEC <=> surface WEC; 4D NEC <=> sigma >= 0 and sigma+p >= 0 (NOT sigma+p >= 0 alone); tangential 2+1 NEC <=> sigma+p >= 0; counterexample sigma=-1, p=2 for nec_holds vs 4D NEC (sat); surface DEC => 4D NEC. later_literature.ref: C. Choi & R.E. Grady, arXiv:2608.09963v1 (2026), Remark 7.6 and p.28
later_literature.what: States the shell NEC/WEC/DEC in the tree's exact form and uses them on Israel layers of Schwarzschild mass interpolations; explicitly calls sigma+p the TANGENTIAL null condition, which is the qualifier the tree omits. Also shows a sigma = 0 layer with p > 0 satisfying the shell NEC/WEC while failing the DEC -- the DEC is strictly stronger, as the tree's reliance on it requires.

later_literature.ref: J.L. Rosa, 'Junction conditions and thin-shells in perfect-fluid f(R,T) gravity', arXiv:2103.11698v2 (2021)
later_literature.what: Uses the same shell energy conditions on sigma and p_t ('all the energy conditions (null, weak, strong and dominant) will be satisfied simultaneously if the surface energy density of the shell is positive' for sigma = 2 p_t) -- consistent with the DEC form sigma >= |p|.

later_literature.ref: M. Visser, S. Kar, N. Dadhich, 'Traversable wormholes with arbitrarily small energy condition violations', arXiv:gr-qc/0301003v2 (2003)
later_literature.what: A GR thin shell of 'quasi-normal matter' that satisfies the WEC and SEC but violates the DEC -- a published instance that the DEC, not the NEC/WEC, is the discriminating shell condition; the tree correctly uses the DEC.

Its type-I NEC 'for all i, rho + p_i >= 0' applied to the 4D distributional shell tensor with zero normal pressure demands sigma >= 0 in addition to sigma + p >= 0; the tree's nec_holds is the tangential NEC only. No consequence for the device (sigma > 0).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: no. This result is a definition (Hawking-Ellis 1973 energy conditions) specialised to a 2+1 surface stress and applied to closed-form Israel values; no measured quantity enters it, so there is no datum the originators could have lacked. The one thing a later reader has that the tree's text does not show is the distinction between the tangential (surface) NEC and the 4D NEC of the distributional tensor -- a matter of statement, not data, and it is already in the literature (Lobo 2007 eq 64 applied with p_n = 0; Choi-Grady 2026 'tangential'). Having it changes nothing here: evidence is the z3 proof that sigma > 0 for every m/R > 0 and that the surface DEC implies the 4D NEC. Evidence the other way (that the definitions themselves are incomplete): pointwise classical conditions are known to be violated by quantum fields (Lobo 2007 sec. II.F.1), but the tree applies them to a classical shell and claims nothing quantum, so that limitation is scope, not error.
grade_evidence: The DEC the verdict rests on (stability.py:35-36, 145-147, 304-306) is the published shell DEC (Choi-Grady 2026 Remark 7.6; Lobo 2007 eq 70 restating Hawking-Ellis), and z3 proves it is also exactly the 4D DEC of the distributional shell tensor. The tree's sigma, p are the Lanczos/Israel values (sympy, agree to 1e-14), the printed columns reproduce to 4 s.f., and the claim 'DEC at every compactness tested' is proved for EVERY m/R > 0 (sympy identities + z3). No datum enters. Recorded, not grade-moving, not repaired: nec_holds is the TANGENTIAL shell NEC without that qualifier; as a 4D statement the NEC also needs sigma >= 0 (z3 counterexample sigma=-1, p=2), but sigma > 0 on the whole device family and the DEC implies the 4D NEC, so no conclusion shrinks; 'ORDINARY MATTER' is supported as 'energy-condition-satisfying' and no further; the canonical's :238-239 is the selftest line, the verdict is :303-306. Source read via banked restatements only (alphaXiv quota exhausted this pass); Hawking-Ellis NAMED-NOT-READ.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if nec_holds / the printed NEC column were used as the 4D NEC on a junction with sigma < 0 (e.g. a thin-shell-wormhole or mass-inside/flat-outside junction: M_in = +0.3, M_out = 0 gives sigma = -2.92e-2), since there sigma + p >= 0 does not imply the 4D NEC; or if a later tree claim asserted the DEC along perturbed (beta^2) trajectories without checking it. WRONG only on a shown device configuration with m > 0 where sigma < |p| -- excluded by the z3 proof. OPEN would apply only if the restatements were found to misquote Hawking-Ellis; reading HE sec. 4.3 or Visser 1995 directly (not possible here) would close that residual.
